title: Сценарий артхаусного фильма  (The Arthouse Movie Script)

segments.t: In the corridor, Nagiyev studies a script for an upcoming arthouse movie he desperately wants a role in. When the cooks ask what the film is about, they admit they understand nothing at all, prompting Nagiyev to dramatically describe a scene with Carlos on a raft.
Которых уже никогда не коснется рука.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Oh, is that you?' Weighing in dryly with Fedya, Senya links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'It is a brand-new movie.' Fedya reacts warmly with a sigh, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'I need it for a role.' Highlighting a role at once, Senya chooses "roli" ("role, part") so Fedya gets the point right away.
'That is what I thought.' Reacting naturally at once, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'What kind of movie is it?' Senya checks openly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
'I did not understand a single thing.' Fedya reacts directly with Senya and brings in "ponyal" ("understood", from "ponyat") as the key Russian word here.
'Nothing whatsoever.' Reacting earnestly at once, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'This is not our usual trash.' Fedya continues sharply without any doubt, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'Picture a waterfall.' Addressing a waterfall during the talk, Senya lands on "vodopad" ("waterfall") as the key everyday word here.
'Carlos is lying on the edge of a raft.' Focusing on the side on the spot, Fedya lands on "krayu" ("the side, the edge", built on "kray") to keep the statement grounded.
'Yes, Carlos.' Senya gently uses this direct affirmation toward Fedya using "da" ("yes") — a crisp "da" ("yes") that confirms the point without extra words.
'A cold wind blowing from the shore.' Underscoring a cold wind around Senya, Fedya uses "kholodnyy" ("cold") to carry the main weight of the thought.
Которых уже никогда не коснется рука.
'Which a human hand will never touch again.' Talking about the affect in front of Fedya, Senya pairs the negative word with "ne" ("not"), since Russian naturally doubles its negatives for emphasis.
Которых уже никогда не коснется рука.

That wraps up this scene as nagiyev shows off a script for a new arthouse film he hopes to star in and tries to explain a surreal scene about a man named Carlos on a raft by a waterfall. Until next time!
